title: to_snake_case drops combining marks (they are treated as word separators), so output is not a fixed point
property: snake-casing an already snake-cased string leaves it unchanged (idempotence)
actual: first pass gives "i\u{307}" (standard lowercase of İ), second pass gives "i" because the combining dot U+0307 is not char::is_alphanumeric and is treated as a word separator and discarded
evidence: transform() splits words on !c.is_alphanumeric(); combining marks (category Mn) are not alphanumeric, so they are silently deleted or split words (e.g. NFD "cafe\u{301}" loses its accent). lowercase() itself emits such a mark for İ, so the library produces output that its own algorithm then treats as a separator. Snake case of an already-snake string is expected to be stable, as for all ASCII inputs (which passed).
